title: Functions, graphs and notation
description: A function maps each input to one output; reading f: R^n -> R^m, graphs, and composition.

title: Summation and product notation
description: Sigma notation, index ranges, and rewriting sums as vector/matrix expressions.

title: Exponentials and logarithms
description: exp and ln as inverses, log of products, why ML works in log space.

title: Vectors and vector operations
description: Vectors as ordered lists / arrows, addition, scaling, linear combinations.

title: Dot product, norm and angle
description: Dot product as sum of products and as |a||b|cos(theta); norms; projection.

title: Matrices and matrix multiplication
description: Shapes, the (m,n)@(n,p) rule, row-by-column dot products, transpose.

title: Matrices as linear transformations
description: A matrix is a function that rotates, scales, shears; columns are images of basis vectors.

title: Derivative as rate of change
description: Limit definition, slope of tangent, derivative rules for power, exp, log, sum, product.

title: Numerical differentiation
description: Forward and central finite differences, truncation versus round-off error.

title: Partial derivatives
description: Differentiate with respect to one variable holding the others fixed.

title: Gradient
description: Vector of partial derivatives; direction of steepest local ascent.

title: Chain rule
description: Derivative of a composition; multiply local derivatives along the path.

title: Jacobian and the multivariate chain rule
description: Matrix of partials for vector-valued functions; chain rule as matrix product, with shapes.

title: Gradient descent
description: Iteratively step against the gradient; learning rate, convergence and divergence.

title: Loss functions
description: Mean squared error, cross-entropy, and why they are natural objectives.

title: Layers and forward propagation
description: A dense layer is activation(X W + b); batch shapes; composing layers.

title: Activation functions
description: Why nonlinearity is required; ReLU, sigmoid, tanh, softmax and their derivatives.

title: Backpropagation
description: Reverse-mode application of the chain rule through a layered network, with tensor shapes.

title: Training loop and gradient checking
description: Forward, loss, backward, update; verifying gradients numerically.

title: Automatic differentiation
description: Computational graphs, PyTorch autograd, and validating a from-scratch implementation against it.

title: Linear regression and the normal equations
description: Fit y ~ Xw by least squares; normal equations X^T X w = X^T y; geometric view as a projection.

title: Ridge regularisation
description: Add lambda ||w||^2 to the loss; closed form (X^T X + lambda I)^-1 X^T y; shrinkage and conditioning.

title: Logistic regression
description: Linear model through a sigmoid trained with cross-entropy; gradient X^T (p - y)/N; linear decision boundary.

title: Generalisation, bias-variance and validation
description: Train/validation/test splits, the bias-variance decomposition, k-fold cross-validation, choosing hyper-parameters.

title: k-means clustering
description: Lloyd's algorithm minimises within-cluster squared distance; monotone decrease, local minima, initialisation.

title: Principal component analysis
description: Directions of maximal variance are eigenvectors of the covariance matrix; projection, reconstruction error.

title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
description: Directions a matrix only stretches: A x = lambda x; characteristic polynomial, diagonalisation, symmetric matrices.

title: Singular value decomposition
description: Any matrix factors as U Sigma V^T: rotate, scale, rotate; singular values, low-rank approximation.

title: Probability, conditioning and Bayes' theorem
description: Sample space and events, sum and product rules, conditional probability, independence, Bayes' theorem.

title: Random variables, expectation, variance and the Gaussian
description: Discrete and continuous distributions, mean, variance, covariance, the univariate and multivariate Gaussian.

title: Entropy, cross-entropy and KL divergence
description: Information content, entropy, cross-entropy as expected code length, KL divergence and its link to maximum likelihood.
